finding: GTM account 3ffe588d-e4a1-48bf-83f4-2c425aede793, closed by Jon Snow, live 1 June: 313 shifts posted in June, 45 worked, a 14% fill rate against 81% across the other 39 GTM accounts (by shifts posted in the extract; the lowest of them fills 50%). GTM credits gross value on posted shifts, so the plan credits $41,081 of revenue on $8,100 of net revenue and lifts Jon Snow from 15% to 152% of quota ($721 to $7,883). Slack corroborates the pattern: Jon says he loads shift templates for rural sites; Ops and Forrest Gump find the facility did not ask for the volume.
treatment: New-logo credit withheld in the recommended column (Inputs!B39 = 1, account listed at Inputs!A42). Plan-as-written columns still show it.
why: Would not release without a leadership decision. Worked-shifts-only would release $1,258 of the $9,339; treating the account as Standard net revenue $1,726. Recommend a GTM guardrail from July: posted volume credits only up to a fill-rate floor, and Ops reviews any account filling under half of what it posts before statements go out.

finding: Joiners, leavers and ramp by calendar day: Ron Weasley started 30 June (one day), Tom Sawyer 15 June, Severus Snape left 29 May, Katniss Everdeen 12 June; Frodo Baggins, Gimli, Jay Gatsby, Scout Finch, Percy Jackson and Anna are mid-ramp.
treatment: 7.10 and 7.11 applied by day: floors prorate against quota/30, credit only on dates employed, managers carry the full revenue.
why: A full-month ramp floor or an unprorated statement would pay Ron $4,640 instead of $160, Tom $2,800 more, Frodo $1,120 more, Severus $1,318 (he earns nothing), Katniss $619 more, plus manager roll-ups.

finding: Expansions: 22 accounts have a second Closed Won opportunity dated June.
treatment: Go-live is the earliest Closed Won (7.3); an expansion does not restart the account.
why: Processing per opportunity resets go-live into June and drops the account from the AM's existing book for the month: 25 AMs and managers lose, one SPIFF flips.

finding: Approved credits on accounts that were not yet existing in June: 34 tickets, $8,249.
treatment: Excluded: credits reduce Existing revenue only (7.2, 7.7), and these accounts have no Existing revenue yet.
why: Charged to the future owner they would cut 23 AM and manager numbers and flip Doc Brown's $1,500 SPIFF.
Subtracting them would cut 33 AM and manager numbers by $533 in total.

finding: Hygiene with no June effect in this model: 12 non-won rows carrying a closed_won_date (residue), 11 opportunities live before they were won, 2 Closed Won opportunities dated after the closer left (Severus Snape 16 June, Katniss Everdeen 15 June; both second opportunities on existing accounts), 4 accounts with no shifts in the extract, 59 Slack rows against a dictionary count of 55. Eight Standard accounts post 900 or more shifts a month at 20% to 31% fill: harmless today because Standard pays on margin, but the same pattern under a GTM tag would pay.
treatment: Stage governs (7.3); go-live from Closed Won rows only; Standard accounts pay on margin.
why: Legolas reports a credit on a Negotiation-stage opportunity on his issued statement; nothing in the export supports it, so the statements already sent need reconciling against this model.

finding: HR dates contradict each other and Slack. Jay Gatsby and Scout Finch show ENT AE from 1 May with the SMB role ending 7 June and 31 May (Jay says 8 June). Lord Voldemort shows manager from 1 May (he says 22 June). Walter White shows SMB AE since 2021 (he says he started two weeks before 12 July).
treatment: HR snapshot governs (Appendix A: Current Role decides the plan; the Manager-ID shown held for the whole month). Escalated for HR to confirm effective dates before payroll.
why: Under the plan's own rules a corrected role date changes nothing for Jay, Scout or Voldemort: quota does not prorate for a role change and the manager snapshot holds for the month. The exposure is a leadership choice: paying Jay and Scout's SMB-closed deals at SMB rates would add $11,488; prorating Voldemort's carry from 22 June would cut $2,683. If Walter White's HR start date is wrong, 7.11 and the ramp floor cut his pay by $2,812.

finding: Ramp restarts on promotion or rehire: Anna (ENT AM from 11 May) is floored at $450,000 against a $314,843 book; Percy Jackson at $217,500 against $150,044; Gimli (rehired 4 May), Jay Gatsby and Scout Finch lose accelerator eligibility (Gimli at 120% of quota, Scout at 128%).
treatment: Restart applied as 7.10 reads ('a promotion into a ramped role or a rehire restarts it').
why: If the clock did not restart: Anna $901 less, Percy $899 less with their chains, Gimli $187 more and Scout $339 more from accelerators. Flag as a design issue: a lateral move pays 100% attainment on 70% of a book, and a tenured rep moving teams loses accelerators for two months.

finding: Closers not employed when the deal closed: 194 accounts carry a closed_by_owner_id whose HR start date is after the first Closed Won (189 if Gimli's earlier 2022 to 2024 stint is respected). 8 carry June credit: Tom Sawyer 3, Frodo Baggins 2, Gimli 2, Ron Weasley 1.
treatment: Paid as 7.4 reads: closed_by_owner_id governs as exported. Inputs!B40 = 1 holds it.
why: After ramp floors and 7.11 only Gimli's two accounts, closed in April 2026 during his gap, move money ($1,318 plus roll-ups). Recommend a CRM audit of how closed_by is set on reassignment before July.

finding: GTM shifts posted before the comp month on windows that opened in June (two accounts: Jon Snow, Daenerys Targaryen).
treatment: Recognised in the month the window opens (Inputs!B38 = 1).
why: 7.6 gives F1-30D an upper bound only, so these shifts are in the window, but no earlier statement could have recognised them. Set B38 to 0 to recognise only shifts posted inside the month. About $230 once the flagged account is held.

finding: account_first_worked_shift_date: 49 accounts have no worked shift on the given date; the first observed shift is 1 to 9 days later, which moves window edges.
treatment: Given date used, as the data dictionary instructs ('do not try to infer it').
why: Sized by re-anchoring on the observed date. Worth a question to the app team about how the field is populated.

finding: Blank closed_by_owner_id on two June go-lives (OPP-00411, OPP-00765): $1,432 of F1-30D revenue credits nobody.
why: $184 of commission forgone at the closer rates the accounts' segments imply. CRM fix requested so July does not repeat it.
